newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen extending profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen extending profit-taking.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lighter trade and analysts saw the Thursday fall as the beginning of a deeper profit-taking correction, after the bourse gained 38 percent since mid-December, and stabilised in the last few sessions.
They said the falls might be additionally fuelled by U.S Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Wednesday warning of a possible need to raise interest rates.

"Greenspan's warning provoked the profit-taking as domestic investors fear that big ones will pull out and those who invest globally could close their positions here while limiting their global equity exposure," said Remigiusz Tarka of IB Austria.

Some attractive stocks had risen by 50-70 percent since mid-December and although foreign investors were still finding Poland's overall prospects attractive, it was difficult for them to find shares which were undervalued, analysts said.

They added that upcoming large issues such as Jelfa 100-million-zloty offering and forthcoming paper maker Celuloza Swiecie estimated 200-million zloty offer were likely drawing some capital from the bourse.
The main market's WIG index fell 2.3 percent to 17,824.4, and turnover fell 10.2 percent to 224.6 million zlotys on all three markets as 66 issues fell, 12 rose and 10 were flat.
Some analysts said the expected falls might last several weeks and take the WIG index down by about 10 percent.
Kable trade was suspended after NKT Cables called public tenders for all shares in the firm.
Prochnik jumped 9.3 percent after National Investment Fund (NFI) 12 announced a tender for the firm's shares to increase its stake in Prochnik to 32.9 percent.
Analysts said Espebepe soared 9.6 percent, extending its recent surge on speculation that a March 14 meeting of the ailing firm's creditors might result in a debt write-off deal.
